title: Window-stitching off-by-one causes boundary double-count / transient burst credits
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: We observed transient overage windows where clients were allowed to consume burst credits that should have been blocked when multiple quota windows (per-key minute, per-org hour, per-route day) overlap a boundary. The enforcement path uses a "window stitching" heuristic to reconcile different window lengths across shards; an off-by-one in the stitch math combined with late-committed shard aggregations leads to double-counting at boundaries and temporary under-enforcement.

This ticket tracks investigation, repro, mitigation, and a safe rollout of a correctness fix to the policy evaluation and shard reconciliation code paths. Impact visible on production metrics (see Metrics below).
steps_to_reproduce: Create an org-scoped hourly quota (3600s window) and a per-key per-minute quota (60s window) for the same route.
Send a steady stream of requests that consume near the per-minute quota and simultaneously push aggregated hourly usage close to the hourly limit.
At a minute boundary (t mod 60 == 0) force a shard reassign (simulate shard migration) so one aggregator flushes while another accepts writes.
Observe enforcement decisions returned to client and check accounting records in the shard-aggregator log: double-count of a small subset (1-3%) of tokens across the boundary.
observed_logs: 2026-03-01T12:00:00.124Z shard-agg-12 flush commit_ts=1677676800124 window_floor=1677676740000 counts=[{key:abc, c:58}]
2026-03-01T12:00:00.128Z policy-eval route=/generate org=org-92 key=abc decision=allow reason=per-minute-under; per-hour-raw=3598
2026-03-01T12:00:00.129Z shard-agg-7 accept write commit_ts=1677676800129 counts=[{key:abc, c:5}]
2026-03-01T12:00:00.130Z meter-reconciler stitch_window calc: floor_div(seconds,60) -> off-by-one adjusted=-1 resulting in overlapping contribution for minute boundary
impact: High — temporary bursts of ~0.5-2% of traffic observed with customers seeing >100% of their minute quotas for 1-2 window boundaries per day. Affected customers are primarily mid-tier Dedicated orgs with high shard-churn (autoscaling, rebalancing). Business impact: a handful of customers reported unexpected overages; internal billing pipeline flagged reconciliation alerts leading to manual investigations.
metrics: Increase in per-minute allowance violations: +1.6% at 12:00 UTC on repro days (prod dashboards: billing.minute_violation_rate)
Spike in billing incident tickets correlated with shard rebalances (ops.incident_count tag=shard_rebalance)
root_cause: A combination of (1) window-floor arithmetic in the stitcher using inclusive boundaries while downstream aggregators used exclusive commit semantics, and (2) race between flush commits from an old shard and writes accepted by a new shard during reassign. The stitcher applied an adjustment (-1) when converting long windows into short-window contributions; the adjustment was wrong for exact-boundary timestamps, producing overlapping attribution for a tiny set of requests.
proposed_fix:
1) Correct the stitch math to use consistent half-open [floor, floor+window) semantics across both the policy-eval stitcher and shard-aggregator commit logic. 2) Add a monotonic commit token to flushes so late-commits are rejected or idempotent when applied to the new shard. 3) Add a fast shadow-check in policy-eval that detects >0.5% delta between shadow meter and authoritative shard reply and falls back to conservative deny.

Implementation details: Update stitch_window() in policy/runtime/quota_stitch.go to compute floor = timestamp - (timestamp % window) and explicitly document half-open behavior; change aggregator flush to attach commit_epoch and compare before accepting cross-shard contributions. Unit tests and property tests will drive boundary cases.
design_decisions: Prefer consistency (half-open windows) over permissive behavior: deny on ambiguous overlaps to avoid billing/regulatory exposure.
Avoid synchronous global locks — use commit_epoch tokens to achieve idempotency rather than blocking the write path.
Short-term conservative fallback (shadow-check deny) enabled via feature flag to allow staged rollout.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged release in runtime-1.26 behind ff=billing-window-fix.
Canary: enable for 2 Dedicated customer orgs with low churn for 24h; monitor billing.minute_violation_rate and reconciliation.delta.
Stage: enable for 10% of traffic (region-based) for 48h if canary green.
Full: enable globally after 72h stable, then flip flag to permanent and remove feature-gated shadow-check after 30 days.
Rollback: if violation rate increases or false-denies >0.1%, revert ff and patch with emergency hotfix.
testing_plan: Unit tests for stitch_window edge cases (t exactly divisible by window, t-1, t+1, randomized fuzz with property tests).
Integration tests simulating shard reassign during flush with deterministic fake clocks.
E2E load test on staging with synthetic traffic mimicking Dedicated autoscale churn and traffic peaks.
Shadow rollout in prod with audit logs shipped to billing-audit-s3 for 30d retention.
